_about: Hand-written key points for pyt-anatomy.html (27 Nov 2026, lead). Samples: FMGE recalls, no images; keys checked.
subject: Anatomy
intro: Anatomy in FMGE is mostly applied: which nerve is injured, which structure passes where, what an embryological failure produces. These are the topics that keep coming back, most-asked first, with the one thing to remember about each.

anat.hn.cn.note: Corneal reflex: sensory V1 (trigeminal), motor VII. Taste: anterior two-thirds by chorda tympani (VII), posterior third by IX. Gag reflex: IX in, X out. Parasympathetic: III (eye), VII (lacrimal, submandibular, sublingual), IX (parotid), X (thorax and abdomen). Trochlear is the only nerve leaving the back of the brainstem.
anat.hn.cn.why: The cornea's sensation comes from the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve.

anat.ul.ni.note: Winged scapula: long thoracic nerve (serratus anterior). Wrist drop: radial nerve (spiral groove, humerus shaft fracture). Claw hand: ulnar (medial epicondyle). Ape thumb and loss of pinch: median (carpal tunnel, supracondylar fracture). Loss of shoulder abduction after neck of humerus fracture: axillary nerve.
anat.ul.ni.why: Winging of the scapula comes from serratus anterior paralysis (long thoracic nerve).

anat.ost.skull.note: Foramen ovale: mandibular nerve, accessory meningeal artery, lesser petrosal nerve, emissary vein (MALE). Foramen spinosum: middle meningeal artery. Foramen rotundum: maxillary nerve. Jugular foramen: IX, X, XI and the internal jugular vein. Superior orbital fissure: III, IV, V1 branches, VI.

anat.hn.lar.note: All intrinsic laryngeal muscles are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve except the cricothyroid (external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve). Posterior cricoarytenoid is the only muscle that opens the cords. Above the cords, sensation is by the internal laryngeal nerve; below, by the recurrent.
anat.hn.lar.why: The superior laryngeal nerve's external branch supplies the cricothyroid.

anat.emb.ug.note: The ureteric bud forms the ureter, pelvis, calyces and collecting ducts; the metanephric mesoderm forms nephrons. Failure of the ureteric bud = renal agenesis. Horseshoe kidney is trapped under the inferior mesenteric artery. Müllerian ducts form the uterus and tubes; Wolffian ducts the male ducts.
anat.emb.ug.why: Without the ureteric bud the kidney never forms: renal agenesis.

anat.emb.pa.note: Pouches: 1st, middle ear and auditory tube; 2nd, tonsil; 3rd, inferior parathyroids and thymus; 4th, superior parathyroids and ultimobranchial body. DiGeorge syndrome (3rd and 4th pouches): low calcium and no thymus. Arches: 1st (V), 2nd (VII), 3rd (IX), 4th and 6th (X).
anat.emb.pa.why: The third pharyngeal pouch forms the inferior parathyroids and the thymus.

anat.neuro.bs.note: Midbrain: III and IV nuclei, red nucleus, substantia nigra. Pons: V, VI, VII, VIII. Medulla: IX, X, XI, XII. Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: PICA, crossed sensory loss, hoarseness, Horner. Medial medullary: XII palsy with opposite hemiplegia.
anat.neuro.bs.why: The red nucleus lies in the midbrain.

anat.neuro.sc.note: Blood supply: one anterior spinal artery (front two-thirds) and two posterior spinal arteries. The cord ends at L1-L2 in adults (L3 in newborns). Brown-Séquard: same-side weakness and loss of position sense, opposite-side loss of pain and temperature. Anterior cord syndrome spares dorsal columns.
anat.neuro.sc.why: The anterior spinal artery supplies the front two-thirds of the cord, the larger part.

anat.ll.ni.note: Foot drop: common peroneal nerve, injured at the neck of the fibula. Deep peroneal: loss of feeling in the first web space. Trendelenburg sign (hip drops on the other side): superior gluteal nerve (gluteus medius and minimus). Tibial nerve: loss of plantar flexion, numb sole.
anat.ll.ni.why: Numbness in the first web space with weak toe extension is a deep peroneal nerve lesion.

anat.neuro.bl.note: Middle cerebral artery: lateral surface of the hemisphere (face and arm motor and sensory areas, speech). Anterior cerebral: medial surface (leg, paracentral lobule). Posterior cerebral: occipital lobe (vision). Lenticulostriate branches of the MCA supply the internal capsule; they bleed in hypertension.
anat.neuro.bl.why: The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral surface of the frontal lobe.

anat.abd.ing.note: The deep ring is a gap in the transversalis fascia, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; the superficial ring is in the external oblique. Contents: spermatic cord in males (round ligament in females), ilioinguinal nerve. Hesselbach triangle (direct hernias): inferior epigastric vessels, lateral edge of rectus, inguinal ligament.
anat.abd.ing.why: In males the spermatic cord runs through the inguinal canal.

anat.emb.gi.note: The dorsal pancreatic bud forms the head (upper part), neck, body and tail; the ventral bud forms the lower head and uncinate process and the main duct. Annular pancreas: ventral bud wraps round the duodenum. Meckel diverticulum: rule of 2s, remnant of the vitello-intestinal duct.
anat.emb.gi.why: The dorsal bud forms the neck, body and tail of the pancreas.

anat.neuro.cbl.note: The cerebellum controls balance and coordination on the same side. Vermis: trunk and gait; hemispheres: limbs. Inferior cerebellar peduncle carries input from the spinal cord; superior peduncle carries output. Signs of damage: ataxia, intention tremor, nystagmus.
anat.neuro.cbl.why: The cerebellum coordinates movement and balance.

anat.thor.heart.note: Right coronary artery supplies the SA node (about 60%) and AV node (about 80%, right dominance), inferior wall. Left anterior descending: front of the septum and anterior wall. Circumflex: lateral wall. The coronary sinus drains into the right atrium.

anat.hn.parotid.note: Parasympathetic supply: glossopharyngeal nerve (lesser petrosal) via the otic ganglion to the auriculotemporal nerve. The facial nerve divides inside the gland into 5 branches but does not supply it. Stensen duct opens opposite the upper second molar.
anat.hn.parotid.why: The parotid's secretory fibres come from the glossopharyngeal nerve through the otic ganglion.

anat.abd.perit.note: Retroperitoneal organs (SAD PUCKER): suprarenals, aorta and IVC, duodenum (2nd to 4th parts), pancreas (except tail), ureters, colon (ascending and descending), kidneys, oesophagus, rectum. The epiploic foramen (Winslow) joins the greater and lesser sacs.
anat.abd.perit.why: The ascending colon is retroperitoneal; the transverse and sigmoid colon have a mesentery.

anat.ul.bp.note: Roots C5-T1. Upper trunk injury (Erb palsy, C5-C6): waiter's tip position, after a difficult birth or a fall on the shoulder. Lower trunk (Klumpke, C8-T1): claw hand, possibly Horner syndrome. Musculocutaneous, median, ulnar, radial and axillary are the main terminal branches.

anat.ul.sh.note: The most mobile and most often dislocated joint (anterior dislocation; risk to the axillary nerve). Rotator cuff: supraspinatus (starts abduction, most often torn), infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis. Sprengel deformity: a high, small scapula that limits abduction.
anat.ul.sh.why: An undescended, high scapula (Sprengel deformity) limits shoulder abduction in a child.

anat.thor.med.note: The superior vena cava is formed by the two brachiocephalic veins; the azygos vein drains into it. Posterior mediastinum: oesophagus, descending aorta, thoracic duct, azygos veins, vagus nerves. Thymus in the anterior mediastinum.

anat.neuro.ic.note: The posterior limb carries the corticospinal fibres to the body; the genu carries corticobulbar fibres. A small bleed or lacunar infarct here (lenticulostriate arteries) causes complete hemiplegia on the opposite side, face, arm and leg equally.

anat.abd.liver.note: Falciform ligament attaches the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and carries the ligamentum teres (old umbilical vein). The bare area touches the diaphragm. Couinaud divides the liver into 8 segments by portal and hepatic veins; the caudate lobe (segment I) drains directly into the IVC.
anat.abd.liver.why: The falciform ligament attaches the liver to the anterior abdominal wall.

anat.thor.dia.note: Openings: IVC at T8 (with the right phrenic nerve), oesophagus at T10 (with the vagal trunks), aorta at T12 (with the thoracic duct and azygos). Phrenic nerve C3-C5. Oesophageal narrowings from the incisors: 15 cm (cricopharynx), 25 cm (aortic arch and left bronchus), 40 cm (diaphragm).
anat.thor.dia.why: The constriction about 40 cm from the incisors is where the oesophagus passes through the diaphragm.

anat.hn.orbit.note: Lateral wall: zygomatic bone and greater wing of sphenoid (the strongest). Medial wall: thin lamina papyracea of the ethmoid (infection spreads into the orbit). Floor: maxilla (blow-out fractures). LR6 SO4: lateral rectus by VI, superior oblique by IV, the rest by III.
anat.hn.orbit.why: The lateral orbital wall is formed by the zygomatic bone and the greater wing of the sphenoid.

anat.emb.heart.note: Fetal shunts: ductus venosus (bypasses the liver to the IVC), foramen ovale (right to left atrium), ductus arteriosus (pulmonary trunk to aorta). After birth they become the ligamentum venosum, fossa ovalis and ligamentum arteriosum. Septum defects and tetralogy come from abnormal septation.
anat.emb.heart.why: The ductus venosus carries placental blood past the liver straight to the IVC.

anat.ost.vert.note: Atlas has no body; the axis has the dens, held against the atlas by the transverse ligament. Typical cervical vertebrae have foramina transversaria (vertebral artery, from C6). Lumbar puncture between L3-L4 or L4-L5 (below the cord's end).

anat.hist.slides.note: Know a few classic slides: thyroid (follicles with colloid), adrenal (cortex layers and medulla), kidney (glomeruli, brush-border PCT), liver (lobules round central veins), lung (alveoli), skin (thin vs thick), oesophagus vs trachea vs stomach linings.

anat.ll.knee.note: ACL stops the tibia sliding forward (anterior drawer and Lachman tests); PCL stops it sliding back (posterior drawer). The medial meniscus is fixed to the medial ligament and torn more often. Unhappy triad: ACL, medial collateral and medial meniscus. Popliteus unlocks the knee.
anat.ll.knee.why: The posterior cruciate ligament prevents backward movement of the tibia.

anat.hn.cav.note: Inside the cavernous sinus: internal carotid artery and VI nerve; in its lateral wall: III, IV, V1, V2. Spread of infection from the 'danger area' of the face. Carotid-cavernous fistula: pulsating proptosis, chemosis, an orbital bruit, often after head injury.
anat.hn.cav.why: Pulsatile proptosis with chemosis and a bruit is a carotid-cavernous fistula.

anat.ll.glut.note: Gluteus maximus: inferior gluteal nerve (extends the hip, climbing stairs). Gluteus medius and minimus: superior gluteal nerve (keep the pelvis level; Trendelenburg sign if weak). Safe injection site: the upper outer quadrant (to avoid the sciatic nerve).
anat.ll.glut.why: The inferior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus maximus.

anat.hist.epi.note: Simple squamous: alveoli, vessels (endothelium). Simple cuboidal with brush border: proximal tubule. Simple columnar: stomach, intestine. Pseudostratified ciliated: trachea. Transitional (urothelium): bladder. Stratified squamous: skin (keratinised), oesophagus (non-keratinised).
anat.hist.epi.why: The proximal tubule is lined by cuboidal cells with a tall brush border (microvilli).

anat.neuro.bg.note: The basal ganglia are the caudate, putamen and globus pallidus (with subthalamic nucleus and substantia nigra in the circuit). Striatum = caudate + putamen. Lentiform = putamen + globus pallidus. Damage gives movement disorders (Parkinson, chorea, hemiballismus).

anat.ll.ft.note: Femoral triangle: inguinal ligament, sartorius, adductor longus. Contents from lateral to medial: nerve, artery, vein, (empty space), lymphatics (NAVEL). The femoral nerve supplies quadriceps, sartorius and pectineus, not the adductors (obturator nerve).
anat.ll.ft.why: Adductor longus is supplied by the obturator nerve, not the femoral nerve.

anat.hn.scalp.note: Layers: Skin, Connective tissue, Aponeurosis, Loose areolar tissue (the 'danger layer', emissary veins), Pericranium. Bleeding from scalp wounds is heavy because vessels are held open by dense tissue. The back of the scalp is supplied by the greater occipital nerve (C2).
anat.hn.scalp.why: The greater occipital nerve (C2) supplies the back of the scalp.

anat.emb.nt.note: The neural tube closes by day 28; the front (rostral) end closes around day 25, the back end around day 27-28. Failure at the front: anencephaly; at the back: spina bifida. Folic acid before conception prevents most cases; raised AFP in maternal blood and amniotic fluid.
anat.emb.nt.why: Failure of the rostral neuropore to close causes anencephaly.

anat.thor.lung.note: The right lung has 10 segments in 3 lobes; the left about 8-10 in 2 lobes. Inhaled objects go to the right side (the right bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical): standing, to the posterior basal segment; lying on the back, to the superior segment of the lower lobe.
anat.thor.lung.why: An inhaled peanut usually lodges in the right lower lobe, often its posterobasal segment.

anat.abd.stom.note: Lesser omentum runs from the lesser curvature to the liver; greater omentum hangs from the greater curvature. Arteries: left and right gastric along the lesser curve, gastroepiploics along the greater curve, short gastrics to the fundus.
anat.abd.stom.why: The lesser omentum is attached to the lesser curvature of the stomach.

anat.hist.gland.note: Adrenal cortex from outside in: zona glomerulosa (aldosterone), fasciculata (cortisol), reticularis (androgens); then the medulla (adrenaline). Exocrine glands: merocrine (most), apocrine (axillary sweat, breast fat), holocrine (sebaceous).
anat.hist.gland.why: The outermost zone, the zona glomerulosa, makes aldosterone.

anat.abd.portal.note: The portal vein is formed behind the neck of the pancreas by the splenic and superior mesenteric veins. Portosystemic anastomoses (where varices form): lower oesophagus, around the umbilicus (caput medusae), rectum (anorectal), and retroperitoneum.
anat.abd.portal.why: The splenic and superior mesenteric veins join behind the pancreatic neck to form the portal vein.

anat.pelv.pd.note: The pelvic diaphragm is the levator ani (pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus, puborectalis) and coccygeus. Puborectalis keeps faecal continence. Damage in childbirth leads to prolapse and incontinence.
anat.pelv.pd.why: The levator ani is the main muscle of the pelvic diaphragm.

anat.pelv.ut.note: The ureter passes under the uterine artery about 2 cm lateral to the cervix ('water under the bridge'), close to the lateral fornix: at risk in hysterectomy. Supports: cardinal (Mackenrodt) and uterosacral ligaments, and the levator ani.
anat.pelv.ut.why: The ureter runs just below the uterine artery near the lateral fornix, where it can be injured.

anat.ul.ct.note: Through the carpal tunnel: the median nerve and 9 tendons (4 FDS, 4 FDP, FPL). Carpal tunnel syndrome: tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers, worse at night, thenar wasting; Tinel and Phalen tests. Common in pregnancy, hypothyroidism, diabetes.
anat.ul.ct.why: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel.

anat.ll.sci.note: The sciatic nerve (L4-S3), the largest nerve, leaves below the piriformis and divides into tibial and common peroneal nerves, usually above the knee. Injections in the wrong gluteal quadrant can damage it.

anat.pelv.pud.note: Pudendal nerve (S2-S4) leaves through the greater sciatic foramen and returns through the lesser, running in Alcock canal. A pudendal block is given near the ischial spine for childbirth. Supplies the perineum and the external sphincters.

anat.hn.pa.note: The 1st arch gives the muscles of chewing, the 2nd the muscles of facial expression, the 3rd stylopharyngeus, the 4th and 6th the laryngeal and pharyngeal muscles. Pouches 3 and 4 form the parathyroids; their failure causes low calcium in newborns (DiGeorge).
anat.hn.pa.why: The parathyroids come from the 3rd and 4th pouches; their failure gives neonatal hypocalcaemia.
